title: Reading and writing numbers to 20
keyIdea: Reading a numeral means knowing which written mark stands for a count from 0 to 20. Writing means making those digits in the right order: tens on the left, ones on the right. Teen numbers are one ten and some ones — 14 is 1 ten and 4 ones. Swapping digits changes the number: 12 is twelve, 21 is twenty-one.

kid: A numeral is the written mark for a number. 7 means seven things.
Teen numbers have one ten and some ones. 14 is a ten and four ones.
When you write sixteen, put 1 then 6. The left digit is the tens. The right digit is the ones.
Watch out: 12 and 21 use the same digits, but they are different numbers because the places swapped.
adult: CCSS K.CC.3: write numbers from 0 to 20 and represent a number of objects with a written numeral. NC Year 1: read and write numbers from 1 to 20 in numerals. Words: numeral, digit, tens, ones, teen, place value, number line.

Common mistakes: swapping teen digits (12 read as twenty-one); writing 15 as 51; thinking 20 means two ones; treating teen numbers as 'ten and teen' words without linking to 10+n; counting objects but tapping a nearby wrong numeral.
In the lab your child matches dots to numerals, builds a teen with a ten-rod and ones, writes digits on a pad, places a bead on a 0–20 line, picks 12 not 21 for twelve, and reads 16 as sixteen.

familyTip: Write 12 and 21 on two cards. Ask 'which is twelve?' then build each with a bundle of ten straws plus loose ones.

visual.caption: Teen (11–19) or not? Drag each numeral, or tap it and then tap a box.

lab.caption: Flagship lab: match counts to numerals, build teens as ten-and-ones, write digits, place on a 0–20 line, and catch 12/21 swaps.

practice.hint: Count the dots, then find the mark that means that count — not a teen or a ten times bigger.
practice.explain: Seven dots match the numeral 7. 17 is seventeen; 70 is seventy.

practice.hint: Teen numbers have one ten. The other digit tells the ones.

practice.prompt: A ten-rod and {n} ones make which number?
practice.hint: Start at 10, then add the ones.
practice.explain: 10 + {n} = {=10+n}. That is a teen or twenty when {n} is 10.

practice.prompt: The numeral shows 1 ten and {n} ones. What number is it?
practice.hint: Tens digit 1, ones digit {n}. Put them together as a two-digit number.
practice.explain: 1 ten and {n} ones is the number {=10+n}.

practice.hint: Twelve is one ten and two ones — digits 1 then 2.
practice.explain: Twelve is 12. 21 is twenty-one; 20 is twenty.

pool.explain: 20 is two tens and zero ones — twenty.

pool.hint: Read tens, then ones. Do not swap.

choices: the digits sit in different places
pool.hint: Place value: left is tens, right is ones.
pool.explain: Same digits, different places: 12 is twelve, 21 is twenty-one.

pool.prompt: Bead on a 0–20 line at ten and {n} ones. Where is it?
pool.hint: Find ten on the line, then count on {n} more ones to the right.

pool.prompt: You count {n} objects. Which numeral do you write?
pool.hint: The numeral is the same count you just made.
Teen numbers are the numbers from eleven to nineteen only.
pool.explain: 15 is fifteen, a teen. 20 is twenty; 8 is a single digit.

pool.hint: In a two-digit number the left place is tens.
pool.explain: In 18 the 1 means 1 ten; the 8 means 8 ones.
